teaser: 188 articles read as 5,664 anchored claims and joined: a frame of 26 ideas, eight clusters, one cut, the peaks, and ten predictions scored, two held, four missed.
core_idea: Reading every article a second time as its claims, names and sources, joined under one grammar, gave a real join, 342 shared ids and 95% of claims joined, and the first thing that emerged was a frame of 26 ideas in more than a quarter of all articles rather than a dimension; with the frame set aside the names fall into eight clusters and one cut, control against the record with control the smaller side and the people, products and method as the bridges, and the editor's hand-drawn desks mostly hold; of the ten predictions two held, four in part and four missed, the misses being that the owner states more than he hedges and the readers were more exact than allowed for.

nodes.label: Built, in 9.5 seconds
nodes.summary: 188 files, 5,664 claims each anchored to a verified quote, 543 pages and seven JSON files under /graphs/.

nodes.label: Twelve readers in parallel
nodes.summary: Sessions of one model, sixteen articles each, half an hour, 4.3 million tokens, the validator as the one checker.

nodes.label: The newsroom states, it does not hedge
nodes.summary: 2,629 facts, 995 data points, 798 limits, 518 proposals, 233 hypotheses, 42 questions; backs 1,396, contradicts 13.

nodes.label: The join is real
nodes.summary: 342 ids in two or more articles against 48 shared labels before; 95% of claims about something another article shares.

nodes.label: A frame of 26 ideas
nodes.summary: The owner, the vault, provenance, RiskMandate, the memo, the behaviour policy, sgit and nineteen more, in a quarter of all articles.

nodes.label: With the frame in, two blobs
nodes.summary: Modularity 0.26 and everything a satellite; without it, eight clusters at 0.42.

nodes.label: Eight clusters
nodes.summary: The vendors and the risk, the newsroom's method, strategy, memory and policy tooling, regulation and Europe, the browser and the keys, governance as a graph, journalism as intelligence.

nodes.label: The editor's layers mostly hold
nodes.summary: Four desks of five at 73% or more in two clusters; the publishers' section and the personas where the clusters put them.

nodes.label: Control against the record
nodes.summary: One cut two ways, agreeing on 88% of nodes; control the smaller side at 43%.

nodes.label: The bridges are the people and the method
nodes.summary: The owner, RiskMandate, provenance, sgit, Claude and fractal graphs; not the behaviour policy and the vault, which anchor opposite sides.

nodes.label: The peaks, and the surprise
nodes.summary: Seven of eight predicted names; the surprise is the owner, the memo and the agents' writing at the top.

nodes.label: The vocabulary is full
nodes.summary: The 30 newest articles add one concept each; the spine was born before September.

nodes.label: Five dimensions, found as designed
nodes.summary: Claims, names, sources, time, the editor's layers; gravity and clusters are the names counted; the peaks needed new words.

nodes.label: Two held, four partly, four missed
nodes.summary: The content was more stated and older than predicted; the readers were more exact: ten quotes refused of 5,664.

nodes.label: The next run's brief
nodes.summary: Anchors for 61 pages, the normaliser, the twins cut at the body, a list value and an evidence level, more seeds; and expectations to score.

figures.caption: The newsroom's names and ideas, cut in two. Every name and idea that two or more articles share, placed left to right by its position along the graph's own Fiedler vector and up and down by a force layout, sized by the articles it is in. Amber is the control side (memory, Anthropic, risk acceptance, blast radius, agent tooling, regulation), teal the record side (privacy, the brief, the publishing method, the reading meter, personas, custom interfaces); grey is the frame, the 26 names and ideas in more than a quarter of all articles, left out of the cut and sitting where the two sides meet. The live version, with a force layout, the clusters and a turn in three dimensions, is at /graphs/map.html.

The same graph, turned: a force layout in three dimensions on a canvas in the page, with no library, coloured by the cut. The two sides are two clouds that meet in the middle; the frame is the pale core. It turns on its own on the map page, and the reader can drag it.

The peaks: the names and ideas with the most gravity that also bridge the clusters, scored by articles times clusters touched. Teal bars are ideas, amber bars are names; the number after the dot is the clusters the node reaches through the articles it shares. The top of the ridge is the frame; the first peak below it is encryption and keys.

What each article added, in publication order from August to 18 October. Grey bars are the names and ideas new to the newsroom in that article; teal bars are those a later article also used. The tallest bars are the early articles, when everything was new; the newest articles add one or two, and few of those are used again.

The dimensions as the run found them, with what each holds: the article, the claims, the names and the vocabulary, the sources, time, then gravity, the frame, the clusters and the cut as the same dimension counted, the peaks as the one layer that needed new words, and the editor's layers scored. The counts are from the report the build writes.

The ten predictions made in the brief, each with what the run found and a score: held when the number is in the range or the shape is as described, partly when the direction held and a number or a name did not, missed when the number was outside the range. Two held, four in part, four missed; the two that missed hardest missed in the run's favour.
